IPSEC_SOCKI_PipeMsg -> IPSEC_SOCKI_HandlePipeData -> IPSEC_SOCKI_PipeData
-> IPSEC_SOCK_ProcPipeData -> IPSEC_SOCK_Buffer_Packet

## Key Evidence
- L25491: VRP_Malloc_F(RAW_U64(ctx_base, 28), ...) -- tainted heap base as first arg
- L25493-25496: list_node[0/1] writes to attacker-controlled address
- L26660: IPSEC_SOCK_ProcPipeData calls IPSEC_SOCK_Buffer_Packet with ctx_base
- L26835: ctx_base comes from external pipe message (INPUT-1)

## Conclusion
Attacker controls ctx_base via pipe message injection, which leads to controlled
heap allocation base. No validation exists on the heap base parameter.
